description: Geological Survey Ireland publishes the locations of geotechnical site investigations and boreholes that engineering companies have submitted to it, through its open data hub. The hub page read on 2026-09-28 explains that site investigations are mapped as polygons carrying the report number, title, town, county and a link to a PDF of the full report, and boreholes as points with coordinates, depth and whether bedrock was reached; typical boreholes are up to 30 metres deep and trial pits up to 4 metres. The hub also offers derived products for particle size analysis, plasticity and in-situ permeability as downloadable zip files, a web viewer, and links to the GeoUrban and three-dimensional geology collections. Coverage is Ireland, wherever investigations were submitted. Access is free, and the hub items state that data produced directly by GSI may be used under CC BY 4.0; terms for the contractor reports themselves were not read. Caveats: coverage reflects where construction happened, and test results sit mainly in scanned reports. It supports ground hazard and resilience studies, such as screening soil conditions for a road embankment or flood defence. Related records: the BGS National Geotechnical Properties Database and GSI's fundamental geospatial data.
